prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Conroe, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1447; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, so you can use the placeholder [PLAINTIFF].

Q: That's fine. Where do you currently live?
A: In the Conroe area, north of Houston.

Q: Let's talk about the accident. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was in a grocery store parking lot in Conroe. I had just parked and was walking toward the entrance.

Q: What time of day was it?
A: It was late afternoon, maybe around five, and the lot was pretty busy.

Q: Describe what happened.
A: A white pickup backed out of a space without looking. I saw it coming at the last second, and I tried to step back, but it clipped the rear quarter panel of my car. The impact jolted me forward and then back.

Q: Did you hit anything inside your vehicle?
A: My head snapped back against the headrest and then forward. I felt a sharp pull in my neck right away.

Q: Did you go to the hospital that day?
A: No, I didn't go right away. I drove home because I thought I was just shaken up. By that evening the stiffness was getting worse.

Q: What treatment have you received since?
A: I saw my primary care doctor about a week later. She diagnosed a neck strain and referred me to physical therapy. I've been going twice a week since then.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes. The therapist has me doing exercises at home too, and I've been using heat packs and taking over-the-counter pain relievers when it flares up.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Mostly with simple things. I can't turn my head fully to check blind spots when I drive, and I had to stop going to my weekly yoga class. Sleeping is harder because I wake up with pain if I roll onto my side.

Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I work at a desk job, so I was able to keep working, but I had to take a couple of afternoons off for appointments and I couldn't type for long stretches without my neck getting sore.

Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior neck problems?
A: No, not that I can recall. I had normal range of motion and no regular pain.

Q: Have you had any other injuries or accidents since then?
A: No, nothing I can think of.

Q: Thank you. Let's take a short break.
